correctness.rationale: The stationary Poisson age folds exactly into an exponential phase density; the score is affine in phase, and its variance is an exact upper bound for every POVM by conditional Jensen. Alternating local y/z readouts recover the full phase almost surely, and bounded L2 martingale convergence attains the bound. z-only observations identify only a reflected phase; conditional variance yields the strict gap, while uniform small-rate expansions give the constants. The finite-N count and independent-clock formulas are elementary integrals. An independent density-matrix QFI reconstruction and 320 finite numerical diagnostics in verify.py checked representative parameters; the analytical steps, not the finite tests, establish the infinite claims.

value.rationale: A single globally shared reset age destroys extensive precision growth even when many individually readable quantum probes are available. An exact quantum Fisher ceiling is achieved with two fixed local bases and exposes a sharp information collapse of population-only z readouts at small reset rate: finite nonzero optimal information against quadratic vanishing restricted information. The contrast with independent clocks identifies the physical mechanism and informs realistic choices of readout resources; it is not a generic textbook inequality alone.
